title: You’re not just struggling.
paragraphs: And deep down… you’re tired of pretending God doesn’t see it.

The thing you buried.
The habit you renamed.
The sin you manage instead of surrender.
But here’s the tension you can’t escape:
If Christ is above all… then He is above that, too.
Even the thing you think disqualifies you.
We live in a world that teaches you how to curate your image, not crucify your flesh.
So you learn to smile while rotting inside.
You raise your hands in worship… but lower your eyes in private.
You say “I’m blessed,” but your soul whispers, “I’m bound.”
You’ve convinced yourself this is normal Christianity.
Some of you reading this know exactly what I’m talking about.
The secret sin no one applauds—but no one confronts.
The pride that masks itself as confidence.
The bitterness you justify because of what they did.
“As long as nobody knows… I’m okay.”
As long as sin sits on the throne of your heart… you are not free.
Because whatever is above your obedience is your master.
And if Christ is not above all in your life… something else is.

“For by Him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities—all things were created through Him and for Him. And He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.”
That means Jesus is not just Savior.

Above your desires.
Above your impulses.
Above your secrets.
Some scholars interpret this passage as a direct confrontation against false teachings that lowered Christ’s authority. Paul wasn’t suggesting Jesus is important.
He was declaring Jesus is absolute.
So what happens when you keep something “above” Christ in your life?
You shrink Him in your mind.
You reduce Him to a helper… instead of bowing to Him as Lord.
You treat Him like an accessory… instead of surrendering to Him as King.
But because you refused to let Him reign.
Because the same Christ who is above all…
Not to expose you and walk away.
But to rescue you and bring you back.

Romans 3:23 says:
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
But God did not leave the story there.
Because Christ, who is above all…

Colossians 1:13–14 says:
“He has delivered us from the domain of darkness and transferred us to the kingdom of His beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.”
But Jesus didn’t negotiate with your sin.
He crushed it at the cross.
On that cross, your hidden sin was not hidden.
And three days later, He rose.
But to prove that sin no longer has the final word over those who repent and believe.
So here’s the question that cuts deep:
why are you still letting sin sit on the throne?
This is not about behavior modification.
Because you cannot hold onto your sin…
and hold onto Christ at the same time.
One will always take the higher place.
You are not too far gone.
Grace is not afraid of your worst moment.

1 John 1:9 says:
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
Because the One who is above all…
is also the One who invites you close.
Right now, in your own words, talk to Him.
And if you’re ready to stop hiding and start walking in freedom…
From hidden shame to holy freedom—
because Jesus is still above all.
